sovereign_country.strategic_role: 最高信誉财富保护、私人银行合规与楚格州加密谷Web3枢纽

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Turbine-Driven Critical Care Invasive Ventilators

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland-EU Bilateral Agreements I and II

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG), SR 955.0, as amended; Swiss Criminal Code Art. 305bis and 305ter (SR 311.0); FINMA Circular 2023/01 on Money Laundering; Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) Art. 697j-697m (legal entity transparency / UBO records, in force 1 January 2024); Federal Act on the Traceability of Legal Entities and Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each UBO, beneficial owner, and PCD signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for Hague Convention states); Consular Legalization at Swiss embassy for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of parent entity (if any) or equivalent evidence of lawful existence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of parent entity's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and legalized Power of Attorney for the Swiss incorporation fiduciary / representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the principal's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized declaration of beneficial ownership (UBO statement) identifying natural persons holding 25% or more of shares or voting rights, or exercising control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary public and corporate fiduciaries
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal notarization in Switzerland; Apostille not required for domestic instrument

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter from a licensed financial institution confirming the UBO's funding sources and commercial record
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank (parent entity or UBO account bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if issued outside Switzerland; bank-stamped signature

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified source of funds evidence for the CHF 100,000 minimum share capital deposit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss bank receiving the capital block deposit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Swiss bank confirmation letter (no Apostille required); foreign source documents require Apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, directors-delegate and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU consolidated sanctions list, and the Swiss SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) consolidated sanctions and embargo measures; mandatory PEP classification and enhanced due diligence in accordance with AMLA Art. 2a, 4 and 6 and FINMA Circular 2023/01; negative media/adverse information review and ongoing transaction monitoring activation on incorporation; screening must be repeated at any change of controller and on a risk-based rolling basis of at least every 12 months.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix - Zentraler Firmenindex (Central Business Name Index of the Swiss Confederation) with filing via the cantonal commercial register offices (Handelsregisteramt) through the electronic Handelsregister-Cockpit and eGRIS platforms
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name (Firma) must be expressed in a Swiss national language (German, French, Italian or Romansh) or in Latin orthography, cite the legal form (AG or SA) and must not be misleading under Art. 950 of the Swiss Code of Obligations; foreign words are admitted only if generally comprehensible and the entire name is convertible to Latin characters; any non-Latin source name must be transliterated into Latin script before filing.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss / Suisse / Svizzera / Schweizerisch (federal authorization required under the Ordinance on the Protection of Public Marks)
Fonds / Investment Funds (FINMA and cantonal licensing required)
Trust / Trustee (administrative and disclosure review; high AML scrutiny)
Clinic / Hospital / Klinik (cantonal health department authorization required for medical facility terms)
Pharma / Medical / Healthcare when implying Swissmedic approval that does not yet exist
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The cantonal commercial registry issues a preliminary name clearance (Namenvorabklärung) typically valid for 30 days; no statutory extension exists, but a fresh application may be submitted after expiry. Upon formal rejection, the applicant may (1) request a written statement of grounds from the cantonal commercial registrar; (2) file an administrative appeal with the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority (Handelsregisteraufsichtsbehoerde) within 30 days of rejection; (3) further appeal to the Swiss Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht) on points of law; (4) in parallel, amend the proposed firm name and refile with a new preliminary clearance and the same incorporation documents.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted. The registered seat (Sitz) of an Aktiengesellschaft must be a genuine, serviceable Swiss address in the municipality named in the articles of association (Art. 626 para. 2 no. 1 OR); pure mailbox or PO-box seats without any administration are rejected by most cantonal registries. A managed office or fiduciary administrative seat is permissible for holding vehicles, but for a Swissmedic-licensed manufacturer of Class III critical care ventilators, commercial substance requires physical facilities, quality management premises and production or authorized storage in Switzerland or the EEA; a purely virtual seat will not support Swissmedic licensing or ISO 13485 certification and would constitute a misleading registered structure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 70% likelihood of unannounced or scheduled physical inspection within 18 months where Swissmedic GMP/ISO 13485 licensing is exercised; for a non-licensed holding or treasury-oriented AG, physical inspection likelihood drops to 10-15% over a three-year period based on cantonal enforcement practices.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary name clearance (Namenvorabklärung) with the cantonal commercial register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory cantonal fee schedule; typical CHF 250-500; non-refundable

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the Swiss articles of association (public deed of incorporation before a Swiss notary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss notary public of the seat canton
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notarial tariff based on share capital; typical CHF 2,000-3,500 for CHF 100,000 nominal capital; notary plus state fee portion

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the AG in the Swiss Commercial Register (primary entry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register and Swiss Federal Commercial Register Office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Federal tariff CHF 600 under Commercial Register Fees Ordinance (GebV-HReg); cantonal component CHF 200-500; plus official gazette (SHAB) publication fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille certification of the UBO and corporate documentary bundle (4 foreign documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Apostille Authority; Swiss embassy/consulate for consular legalization of non-Hague state documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fee per document; CHF 75-150 per Apostille; consular legalization at applicable Swiss tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of corporate documents, passports and UBO declarations into German (or French/Italian)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark CHF 80-120 per standard page, certified translation with sworn certification stamp

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Establishment and initial completion of the internal UBO register under Art. 697j-697m OR
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Swiss fiduciary / corporate services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark CHF 1,200-2,000 for UBO register setup, identity verification and documentation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and administrative seat services (first year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed fiduciary (Sitzgesellschaft administrator) in seat canton (e.g., Zug, Zurich, Geneva)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark annual fee CHF 5,000-7,000 covering domicile, correspondence handling, statutory mail forwarding and compliance inbox

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: OFAC, UN, EU, SECO sanctions list and PEP screening of 2 UBOs, 2 directors and authorized signatories
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed compliance data provider (LSEG/World-Check or equivalent) and delegated AML officer
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark USD 120-350 per person screened; includes initial negative-media review and 12-month monitoring

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary Swissmedic qualification consultation for Class III invasive ventilator manufacturing licence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swissmedic (Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products) or licensed regulatory consultant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Swissmedic tariff hours plus market benchmark 6-8 hours of regulatory strategy consultation; optional but prudent pre-incorporation stage

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht / OR), SR 220, Articles 620 et seq. (incorporation and governance of the Aktiengesellschaft / AG); Articles 626–635 (formation deed and registered capital); Article 637 (contributions in kind); Articles 698 and 716b (shareholder and board competences).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of the registered office (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug if Zug is selected as the seat); the Swiss Federal Commercial Register (eGRIS) acts as the central public database of all cantonal commercial registries.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised deed of incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde) and commercial register application form (Anmeldung zur Handelsregistereintragung) filed by the notary; registration becomes effective upon publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SOGC / SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The share capital of an Aktiengesellschaft must be at least CHF 100,000. At formation, at least 20% of the nominal value of each share must be paid up, but the aggregate paid-up capital may not be less than CHF 50,000. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked bank account (Sperrkonto) opened in the company's name; the bank confirmation of payment is submitted to the notary and the Commercial Register. The blocked funds are released only upon the company's registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At the constitutive meeting, the founding board unanimously resolved: 1. The issued and subscribed share capital of CHF 100,000 is approved; the bank deposit confirmation shows that CHF 50,000 has been paid up and is at the free disposal of the company. 2. The registered office is fixed at [address], [ZIP] [City], Switzerland. 3. The board appoints [Name] as Chair, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer. The Chair and the CFO each have individual signature; all other directors have joint signature. 4. The board authorises the Chair to execute the registration application and all incidental corporate filings with the Commercial Register Office and tax authorities, and to open business bank accounts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarisation of the Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official civil law notary of the Canton of Zug or the canton of the registered office (Notariat / Etude notariale).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and finalise the Articles of Association (Statuten) containing company name, registered office, purpose, share capital, share class, and governance rules. The founders appear before the notary, who authenticates the deed of incorporation, verifies the identity and capacity of the founders, certifies their signatures, and issues the notarised instrument required for Commercial Register filing.
required_dossiers: Articles of Association (Statuten)
Passport or identity cards of all founders
Declaration of acceptance of office by directors
List of registered shareholders and share allocations
Notarisation instruction sheet
Power of attorney if a founder is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or a commercial register pre-check identifies missing statutory clauses or defective capital requirements, the founders must amend the Articles and execute a corrective notarial deed before onward filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Paid-Up Share Capital and Obtaining Bank Capital Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss bank acting on the company's behalf, e.g., Zuger Kantonalbank or another Swiss commercial bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders open a blocked share-capital account in the name of the company in formation. The minimum paid-up amount of CHF 50,000 is credited to this dedicated account. The bank issues a written confirmation (Bankbestätigung) to the notary stating the amount paid up, the account holder, and the blocking until Commercial Register registration. The confirmation must accompany the registration application.
required_dossiers: Draft deed of incorporation and Articles of Association
Certificate of incorporation availability or name reservation, if obtained
Founder identification documents and beneficial-ownership declarations
Bank account opening forms and source-of-funds evidence
Payment instruction or wire confirmation for CHF 50,000 minimum paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests enhanced due diligence or rejects the economic beneficiary, provide full source-of-funds and shareholder chain documentation; choose an alternative licensed Swiss bank and obtain a new capital confirmation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Application and Statutory Board Resolution Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug / the Commercial Register Office of the canton of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary or an authorised representative electronically submits the commercial register application containing the deed, Articles, capital confirmation, signed appointments, and specimen signatures. The registry checks the capital, legal capacity, company name, and governance provisions. The first board resolution is appended to the filing as confirmatory corporate approval of share subscription, registered office address, and officer appointments. Upon approval, the AG is registered in eGRIS and published in the SOGC.
required_dossiers: Notarised application form for registration of an Aktiengesellschaft
Notarised deed of incorporation
Notarised Articles of Association
Bank confirmation of paid-up share capital
List of directors and authorised signatories with certified specimen signatures
Pro-forma first board resolution approved by the founding directors
Certificate of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cantonal registry practice allows a statutory short cure period for minor omissions. If the application is queried, the notary or applicant must respond within the registry deadline with corrected documents, signature certifications, or an amended capital confirmation. A formal refusal may be appealed to the cantonal administrative court within the statutory appeal period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Corporate Governance Setup and Statutory Books
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Managing board of the AG; external corporate secretary or fiduciary, if appointed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After valid registration, the board must convene, approve the governance regulations, adopt bank signatures, maintain the share register, minute its decisions, archive the incorporation dossier, and ensure the company letterhead, invoices, and contracts state the registered office, company identification (UID sires), and Commercial Register entry details. Corporate governance minutes and regulatory filings are placed under board responsibility.
required_dossiers: Commercial register excerpt in force
Board meeting minutes including the first board resolution and officers' acceptance
Share register and transfer ledger
Bank mandate resolution and authorised signature specimens
Organisational regulations (Organisationsreglement) if adopted
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If deficient statutory books or signature rules are detected, the board must ratify corrective minutes and, where required, file an updated application form with the Commercial Register to record changes of officers or signature rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / FTA), Cantonal Tax Office of Zug, AHV Ausgleichskasse (notably Zug compensation fund), and SUVA industrial accident insurance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Swiss UID (business identification number), register for value-added tax with the ESTV if annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed CHF 100,000, enrol as employer with the cantonal AHV compensation office for old-age and survivors insurance, and conclude compulsory accident and non-occupational accident insurance policies. The tax number and UID must be referred to in all invoices, bank accounts, and supplier contracts.
required_dossiers: Confirmed Commercial Register excerpt
Board resolution appointing the tax representative and payroll agent
Company identification number (UID) obtained from the Federal Statistical Office
VAT registration form (Registrierung Mehrwertsteuer / UID)
Employer registration form for social security (AHV/ALV/EO)
Insurance coverage confirmation for occupational accident insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ESTV or compensation office issues a query, the applicant must respond within the stated deadline by providing formal translations or certified corporate documents. Late submissions may be cured, but ancillary tax penalties can be avoided by obtaining professional fiduciary assistance before the deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Application for Medical Device Establishment Registration and Notified-Body Conformity Assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swissmedic (Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products) and a Swiss designated notified body for the conformity assessment of the Class IIb invasive ventilator; additionally the Cantonal Trade and Industry Office for occupational and plant permits.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the manufacturer establishment registration with Swissmedic under the Swiss Medical Devices Ordinance (MedDO). Implement and, if applicable, certify a quality management system to ISO 13485:2016, prepare the technical documentation, conform with EU MDR 2017/745 requirements or the Swiss MDR equivalence rules, and submit the Class IIb ventilator documentation for conformity assessment. The physical production plant must also be registered with the cantonal trade licensing office for operation.
required_dossiers: ISO 13485 quality management system certificate
Technical documentation including essential requirements checklist and risk management report
Clinical evaluation for the ICU mechanical ventilator in accordance with MDR / Swiss regulations
Post-market surveillance and vigilance procedures
Declaration of conformity and CE marking plan
Factory premises documents and product classification rationale
Swissmedic establishment registration form for manufacturers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Swissmedic or the notified body requests additional testing or clinical data, the manufacturer must complete a technical review, update the technical file, and resubmit within the established review period. Any major deficiency requires a corrective action plan and re-assessment before the product can be placed on the market.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Environmental and Civil Defence Physical Licensing of the Manufacturing Plant
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Office for Trade and Industry (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit), Cantonal Building Inspectorate, Cantonal Environmental Office (Amt für Umwelt), fire police, and SUVA for occupational safety.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the final industrial operating permit (Betriebsbewilligung) for the assembly, testing, and packaging plant; complete the environmental pre-screening under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance; procure fire safety certification and structural load clearance; and obtain the workplace health and safety inspection approval before commencing production. The company must also register as a waste generator for manufacturing waste and, if under SUVA jurisdiction, undergo an accident prevention inspection.
required_dossiers: Building permit and structural certificate of occupancy
Fire safety certification issued by the cantonal fire prevention inspectorate
Environmental preliminary screening and emission declarations
Waste management registration and disposal contracts
Occupational health and workplace inspection documentation
SUVA risk assessment and accident prevention measures
Floor plan of production areas with ventilation and fume extraction layout
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where a permit is refused or queried, the company must submit an engineering revision, updated environmental calculations, or a civil defence compliance plan to the competent office. Formal permit refusals are appealable to the cantonal administrative court; in the interim, production may not lawfully commence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Swissmedic (Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products) for medical device manufacturer registration and market surveillance; the Cantonal Trade and Industry Office (Amt für Wirtschaft und Arbeit) of the canton of the registered production plant and the Cantonal Building/Industrial Inspectorate for the operating permit.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Manufacturer establishment registration and manufacturing operating permit for a medical device production plant under Articles 14 et seq. of the Swiss Medical Devices Ordinance (MedDO) and cantonal Betriebsbewilligung.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / Bundesamt für Umwelt, BAFU), with the Cantonal Office for the Environment (Amt für Umwelt) of the production canton as the lead permitting authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Preliminary environmental screening is mandatory; full EIA is not automatically triggered for a medical device assembly and functional testing plant unless the facility includes surface-treatment processes, organic solvent consumption above statutory thresholds, hazardous-air-emission processes, or other operations listed in Annex 1 of the Swiss EIA Ordinance (UVPV / OEIA).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The facility must comply with the precautionary principle of the Environmental Protection Act (SR 814.01), the air emission limits of the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV / OPair), the water-protection prohibitions of the Waters Protection Act (GSchG), the noise-conflict rules of the Noise Abatement Ordinance (LSV), and the waste handling requirements of the Technical Ordinance on Waste (TVA), in particular for electronic waste, solvent waste, and packaging residues.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before production may start, the company must obtain the cantonal fire safety certification, structural load approval, workplace occupational safety inspection, SUVA accident-prevention certification, and electrical installation approval under the Low Voltage Ordinance. The production plant and all technical devices must be suitable for operation in an ICU device manufacturing environment, including emergency lighting, emergency exits, and fire-safety segregation of test laboratories.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC); official portal: www.estv.admin.ch and e-services via www.e-service.admin.ch
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities must first be registered in the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregister / Registre du commerce) at the cantonal level, obtaining the Swiss Identification Number (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer UID). For VAT purposes, the UID is used as the VAT ID; the entity must apply for VAT registration with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) if taxable turnover in Switzerland exceeds CHF 100,000 per year (excluding VAT). The application is submitted electronically via the e-service portal or by paper form, providing the UID, business purpose, and expected turnover. The ESTV confirms the VAT registration and assigns a VAT number in the format CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX MWST/IVA/IVA. Non-resident entities without a Swiss registered office but with taxable operations in Switzerland must appoint a Swiss fiscal representative for VAT and direct tax filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Switzerland does not operate a check-the-box election system. However, Swiss tax law provides specific elective regimes that may be exercised by an AG: (i) VAT group election (Art. 21 VAT Act) allowing affiliated entities to be treated as one taxable person; (ii) participation deduction election (Art. 69 Federal Act on Direct Taxation) for qualifying dividends and capital gains on qualifying participations, which is applied upon meeting thresholds and subject to confirmation; (iii) possible cantonal tax status electives (e.g., mixed holding or principal company status) that must be formally requested and approved; (iv) Swiss-Hybrid Mismatch Rules (implementing OECD BEPS actions) do not provide elective elections but allow for a modified taxation approach if mismatches are identified; the taxpayer must notify the tax administration of any hybrid arrangement triggering a mismatch.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / TVA / IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 in annual global taxable turnover (excluding VAT); for non-profit/charitable activities CHF 150,000; for certain smaller businesses a CHF 150,000 threshold applies from 1 January 2025 under the revised VAT Act.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping. Electronic invoicing is mandatory for business-to-government (B2G) transactions under the Confederation's procurement rules using the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 format. For B2B transactions, e-invoicing is permitted and encouraged; however, the acceptance of electronic invoices must be agreed contractually. Taxpayers must preserve all invoices and underlying books in a format that is readable and auditable by the tax administration, with a retention period of 10 years. No API-based fiscal clearance mechanism is in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to a destination outside Switzerland are subject to VAT at 0% if the goods are physically transferred to a foreign country and the exporter retains documentary evidence of export (Art. 23(2) VAT Act). Services supplied in connection with exported goods (e.g., transport, insurance) and certain international services (e.g., services abroad, international freight) are likewise zero-rated if provided to a foreign recipient and the recipient provides a declaration of business status. For medical devices such as ICU mechanical ventilators, the exporter must ensure the goods leave Switzerland within a reasonable time (typically 30 days) and must hold corresponding proof of export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Swiss customs export document duly stamped by the Swiss Federal Customs Administration)
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill, CMR road consignment note, or other transport document indicating the destination outside Switzerland)
Inward Remittance Certificate (proof of foreign currency payment received from the overseas customer, or bank statement verifying the receipt of proceeds)
Export Permit (if required under Swiss medical device or dual-use export controls)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Swiss Federal Tax Administration conducts risk-based audits on export zero-rating claims, focusing on completeness of export evidence and timely remittance of proceeds. If the evidence is insufficient or funds are not repatriated within the 180-day window, the VAT at 8.1% is retrospectively payable from the date of the original supply, plus statutory default interest (5% per annum). In cases of fraudulent claims or willful tax evasion, fines are imposed under the Federal Act on Direct Taxation and the VAT Act; administrative penalties can reach 3 times the evaded tax (or up to 5 times in serious cases) and criminal prosecution may lead to imprisonment of up to 5 years. Additionally, the clawback extends to the entire supply chain and the exporter's fiscal representative is jointly and severally liable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains full current- and capital-account convertibility for the Swiss franc (CHF). No exchange controls, no central bank approval for inward/outward transfers, and no legal restrictions on profit or capital repatriation for a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft. Dividends and capital redemptions are freely remittable, subject to the 35% Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) which is reclaimable by treaty-eligible recipients; this is a tax consideration, not an FX restriction. CHF settlement works through SIC/SIC4 and CLS. Practical banking friction arises from post-merger consolidation (UBS/Credit Suisse), banks' elevated KYC documentation demands, and strict privacy/AML balancing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement. The manufacturer may retain 100% of export receivables in foreign currency, maintain multi-currency accounts, convert to CHF at any time, and request conversion via spot or forward transactions. There is no mandatory timeline or conversion ratio. Statutory reporting obligations exist for balance-of-payments statistics: Swiss companies generally report cross-border payment flows above CHF 10 million aggregate per calendar year or individual transactions above CHF 25,000, subject to SNB threshold-based reporting schedules.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating is MEDIUM. FINMA-licensed FinTech companies may take public deposits up to CHF 100 million on a non-interest bearing basis, but a full banking licence is required to provide broad corporate treasury and cross-border financing services. Offshore EMI licences (FCA-UK or EU PSD2) are not passportable into Switzerland; they can only engage on a reverse-solicitation basis without holding Swiss client funds. Zug 'Crypto Valley' licensed banks (SEBA Bank AG, Sygnum Bank AG) provide viable tokenised FX/liquidity rails but are less suitable for heavy government LC confirmation and medical-device trade finance. Therefore, for a Mechanical Ventilator exporter relying on LC and SWIFT wire rails, a domestic commercial bank remains the operational treasury anchor; fintechs are supplementary FX and payment-innovation rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Swiss anti-money-laundering regulation requires banks to identify all legal representatives and beneficial owners. Remote/video identification is permitted in specific low-risk scenarios, but in practice the corporate director and any non-Swiss signatory undergo an in-person interview at the bank's premises at account opening. We mandate at least one physical board presence — the sole director or the appointed Swiss resident authorised signatory — carrying the passport, notarial board minutes, and Swiss Commercial Register excerpt. Remote opening is generally declined for a multi-jurisdictional beneficial ownership structure; the physical interview embedding is the prudent treasury blueprint.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner(s) with opaque or cascading shareholding chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised share ledger; Swiss Commercial Register (Zefix) excerpt; signed beneficial-owner declaration using the Swiss bank standard form; corporate group chart comprising all intermediate entities; investment-fund or trust deed if applicable; source-of-wealth statement; bank reference letter from the remitting bank with six-month transaction history proving the CHF 100,000 statutory minimum share-capital availability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade flows with emerging-market government hospital authorities issuing sovereign or Government LC (MT700)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Confirmed government tender contract and award letter; full LC copy including underlying purchase contract; Ministry of Health-approved end-user attestation; UN/EU/OFAC/SNB sanctions screening snapshots; SECO export licence check for dual-use or controlled goods if the ventilator components appear on the Swiss or EU control list; ECA-backed insurance certificate or correspondence if export risk insurance is deemed necessary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inbound capital injection from tax-uncertain venues exceeding CHF 1 million within the first 12 months
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share subscription agreement or capital contribution resolution; board minutes confirming upward capital increase and commercial purpose; source-of-funds file covering originating bank statements, loan/gift instrument, tax clearance or QRO tax opinion; import/export contract supporting the deployed capital; notarised declaration of no beneficial interest held in a shell-company corridor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant injection of initial share capital (minimum CHF 100,000) into a blocked Capital Escrow Account (Sperrkonto) via SWIFT MT103 using ISO 20022 purpose code CAPT (Capital Contribution) or INVS if accompanied by investment contract evidence. The notarial deed of incorporation, subscribed share list, and bank confirmation of free availability of funds (Freiverfügbarkeit) must be forwarded to the bank prior to transfer execution. Funds remain blocked until the Swiss Commercial Register issues the registration entry; thereafter, the escrow account is converted into an operational current account. No SNB prior approval is required. The remitter legal name must reconcile exactly with the shares subscription schedule, and the beneficial owner/source of wealth statements must predate the wire in the bank's compliance workflow.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary outbound rails: (a) SWIFT MT103 for supplier payments and distributor rebates in USD, EUR, or CNH; (b) SIC/SIC4 Swiss Interbank Clearing for CHF-denominated vendor settlements; (c) government and institutional payment rail: Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700) issued by foreign ministries or central medical procurement agencies, confirmed by UBS or ZKB as advising/confirming bank under UCP600; (d) standby LCs (URDG758) for bid bonds and performance guarantees. Payments under government LCs are routed through the confirming Swiss bank to obtain first-loss protection and clean discounting. For CHF domestic settlements, use the SIX SIC4 real-time rail to avoid systemic drag; for EUR settlements in Switzerland, use SECOM/Swiss Euro Clearing. No ISDA agreement is required for vanilla FX transactions used for trade settlements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla CHF/EUR FX Forward (fully deliverable onshore using CLS/SIC)
Vanilla CHF/USD FX Forward (fully deliverable onshore using CLS/SIC)
FX options on EUR/USD and CHF/USD pairs (European style, premium disclosed, bank ISDA or Swiss Master Agreement required)
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) under ISDA 2002 for long-dated receivable funding
Harmonised index-linked commodity forwards for stainless steel and electronic component procurement cost hedging (strictly subject to underlying trade documentation)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting protocol and shareholder resolutions on the annual financial statements, appropriation of profit, discharge of directors, and election of auditors where applicable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book retained at the registered office; no regulatory filing required for a private AG.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after the balance-sheet date (Art. 699(2) Swiss Code of Obligations); for a 31 December year-end, by 30 June.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors are personally liable for damage caused by delay; shareholders or creditors may petition the competent court to convene the AGM; persistent failure to maintain a valid statutory organ may lead to court measures and eventual commercial-register strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory annual financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, notes, and where required the management report), signed by the Board of Directors.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records at the registered office; filed with the cantonal tax authority in support of the annual corporate tax return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be prepared and signed before the AGM, no later than 6 months after the balance-sheet date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Invalid or incomplete accounts render dividend and distribution decisions unlawful; directors may be liable for damages, and the tax authorities may estimate taxable income and impose administrative fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory audit report (limited audit or ordinary audit opinion) issued by the licensed Swiss audit body.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Presented to shareholders at the AGM; retained in the corporate archive and submitted with the tax declaration when required.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Report must be issued and presented before the AGM, ordinarily no later than 6 months after the balance-sheet date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a legally required auditor can result in court-ordered appointment and, if the defect persists, commercial-register strike-off measures; directors additionally risk personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss corporate income tax declaration covering Federal Direct Tax and Cantonal/Communal Income Tax.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration of the registered seat and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/AFC).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due on 31 March of the following tax year; canton-specific extensions commonly to 30 June or 31 August.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest runs from the effective due date; negligent or intentional late filing attracts fines under federal and cantonal tax law up to CHF 10,000 and may trigger enforced collection measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Swiss VAT reconciliation and settlement statement covering all taxable supplies and input VAT deductions.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Return and tax payment are due within 60 days after expiry of the VAT period; for an annual period ending 31 December, the annual settlement is due by 31 March.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest accrues on the unpaid balance; summary penalties of up to CHF 8,000 for negligent conduct and higher penalties or penal proceedings for intentional evasion may be imposed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer annual payroll and social insurance declaration, including AVS/AI/EO, ALV, BVG and occupational pension data.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Statutory compensation office / social insurance administration (Ausgleichskasse).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual Lohnausweis and employer declaration must be delivered by 30 January of the next year or the electronic deadline fixed by the compensation office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late declaration interest and employer liability for unpaid social contributions; negligent or erroneous declarations attract administrative fines under Swiss social insurance law.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A limited audit is compulsory if the AG exceeds two of the following thresholds in two consecutive fiscal years: total assets CHF 10 million, net turnover CHF 20 million, average workforce 50. An ordinary audit is compulsory if it exceeds two of: total assets CHF 20 million, net turnover CHF 40 million, average workforce 250, or is a listed, prudentially supervised, or significant group company. A private AG may dispense with audit only by unanimous shareholder consent if the limited-audit thresholds are not exceeded.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting rules (Art. 957 ff. CO) supplemented by Swiss GAAP FER; IFRS is mandatory for listed companies and otherwise permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No statutory annual UBO restatement is required. The share register must remain accurate at all times; beneficial-owner particulars are verified and confirmed on each share transfer and updated without delay upon any acquisition. Material beneficial-ownership changes, where applicable, must be notified to the relevant Swiss transparency register within the prescribed period.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% federal corporate income tax levied on post-tax profit (effective federal burden on pre-tax profit: 7.83%); combined federal + cantonal + communal effective statutory burden approximately 14.6% in the preferred Zug base and 11.9%–21.0% across German/French cantons
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified patent/IP box: 90% exemption of qualifying IP-derived net income (nexus-based); R&D super-deduction: up to 150% additional deduction in progressive cantons (e.g., Zug, Zurich, Basel-Stadt; may be limited for R&D contracted to related parties); notional interest deduction on new qualifying equity in certain cantons; cantonal tax holidays up to 10 years for new manufacturing companies in selected cantons; participation relief for dividend income from substantial foreign subsidiaries (95–100% exemption); Pillar Two Qualified Domestic Minimum Top-Up Tax (QDMTT) at 15% applicable to Swiss groups with revenue ≥ EUR 750 million from FY 2024

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Unified cantonal/federal corporate tax return (Steuererklärung juristische Personen / Déclaration fiscale pour personnes morales) filed by the AG's legal representative; submitted via the canton's official e-filing portal (canton Zug: TaxOnline/eSteuererform; most cantons: SwissTax / eTax systems), with automatic forwarding to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for federal direct tax purposes; UID number (UID CHE-xxx) is the mandatory access key
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, declaration must reach the cantonal tax authority by 31 March of the following year (30 June if filed electronically with request for extension); off-calendar fiscal year (e.g., 31 January year-end): due within 3 months after the annual general meeting or at the latest 6 months after fiscal year-end; interest-bearing reminders apply after expiry

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, registered seat, UID number, Swiss Tax ID (CH-Nr.), capital stock, board members and authorized signatories
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete for the Swiss resident AG only; non-resident shareholders are not required to file, but their legal name, seat and jurisdiction must be disclosed in the shareholders appendix for WHT purposes

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Tax period and balance sheet date
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the business year, changes in fiscal year, opening and closing balance sheet totals
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align with the annual statutory financial statements; no non-resident parallel reporting

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Net profit per income statement (Handelsgewinn)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit before taxes per audited financial statements, including extraordinary income and value adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Incidental foreign branch income must be allocated under the Swiss PE rules and reported on the same form

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add non-deductible expenses (federal/cantonal income taxes, hidden profit distributions, exaggerated director fees, bribes and criminal fines); deduct tax-free income (participation income, IP box, capital gains on qualifying shareholdings)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Hidden distributions to a non-resident parent (non-arm's-length intercompany pricing) are recharacterized as deemed dividends subject to 35% WHT on top of the corporate adjustment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying IP income (patents and comparable rights used in the ICU ventilator manufacturing process) reduced by a 90% nexus-capped exemption; deduction only if qualifying R&D is carried out in the Swiss entity or Swiss contractor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Acquired-patent income only eligible if enhancement expenditure in Switzerland meets the nexus fraction; the non-resident group must supply cost-contribution evidence on request

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional deduction of up to 50% of wage and third-party R&D costs (Zug: up to 150% total deduction) for internal R&D on ventilators and related medical software; capped by canton-specific ceilings
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: R&D contracted to a related foreign entity does not qualify; user documentation prepared under the OECD TP guidelines must be kept available

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unrelieved prior-year losses offset against net taxable income; statutory relief period of 7 years
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of the Swiss branch of a foreign parent are not attributable to the AG; change-of-ownership clauses (Art. 67 DBG) can forfeit relief after a qualifying restructuring

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Tax credits for foreign source income and withholding taxes
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unilateral credit (ordinary and per-category limitation) for foreign withholding taxes on foreign business income; DTA credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident shareholder cannot credit the Swiss 35% WHT in the Swiss return; it must claim refund/reduced rate under the applicable DTA in its own tax return

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: procedural fine up to CHF 1,000 (Art. 177 DBG); assessment by estimation and a waiting surcharge; late payment interest at 3% p.a. on the unpaid federal/cantonal tax; failure to submit statutory books: fine up to CHF 10,000; tax evasion (intentional false or incomplete declarations): surcharge up to 3 times the evaded tax; tax fraud (falsification of books): imprisonment up to 3 years or fine

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: VAT return (MWST-Abrechnung / Déclaration TVA) via the ESTV AS1 electronic portal; the AG acts as a taxable person for supplies of ICU ventilators and spare parts, irrespective of export exemption
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly (or semi-annual for taxable turnover below CHF 500,000; annual for turnover below CHF 100,000 if registered)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 60 days after the end of each calendar quarter/settlement period; balance and payment due simultaneously; automatic reminders only in the event of default
tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file: fine up to CHF 8,000; VAT evasion: fine up to 4 times the evaded tax and, in serious willful cases, imprisonment up to 3 years (Art. 103–105 MWSTG); directors jointly liable when the company is unable to pay (Art. 12 MVSTG)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Withholding tax declaration (Verrechnungssteuerabrechnung) filed with the ESTV via the ‘e-verrechnungssteuer’ portal; mandatory when the AG distributes dividends, interest on bonds or loans from Swiss sources
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 days after the end of the quarterly settlement period (31 January / 30 April / 31 July / 31 October); tax on deemed distributions (hidden profit distributions) is due when detected by audit
tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Unpaid WHT: statutory claim against the debtor plus interest at 3%; where the company is liquidated or insolvent, the responsible board members are personally pursued; withholding omission penalties and criminal charges for intentional non-declaration (Art. 174 DBG applies to the federal tax)

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) is deducted at source by the AG on all dividends (including hidden distributions and repurchases) paid to shareholders; Swiss-resident corporate shareholders receive a full refund; non-resident shareholders receive a refund of the excess over the applicable DTA rate
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain the reduced treaty rate (e.g., 0% for an EU parent with ≥25% shareholding held 2 years under the CH-EU agreement; 5% under most OECD DTAs with a 10–25% participation threshold; 15% portfolio), the non-resident shareholder must file the official refund claim (Form 82) with the ESTV within 3 years of the distribution; submission package: tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the home tax authority (not older than 3 months), a certification of beneficial ownership, the dividend payment notice and shareholding evidence; the AG should apply the full 35% rate at payment and the shareholder reclaims after qualification; alternatively, the simplified notification procedure is available for listed securities only
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% Swiss WHT under domestic law (no source withholding) and 0% under most Swiss DTAs; interest: 0% WHT on ordinary bank and commercial debt interest; 35% WHT applies only to interest on Swiss bond-type instruments and money market paper; treaty rates for interest generally 0–10% (e.g., 0% for bank loans, 10% for other debt under older DTAs); the AG must nevertheless document deductibility and arm's-length interest rates under Art. 58 DBG

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory when annual cross-border related-party transactions (goods, services, financing) exceed CHF 5,000,000; Master File: mandatory when the group's consolidated global turnover exceeds CHF 850,000,000 (ESTV TP documentation circular, OECD-aligned 2020/2023); the ICU ventilator manufacturer must also retain a benchmarking study for its RoHS/export prices to related distributors in Europe and Asia
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price), Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method), Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland applies a functional substance doctrine though not an ESR-style licensing code: treaty benefits, patent box relief, notional interest deduction and tax rulings all require real economic activity, payroll, premises and management in Switzerland; a pure shell AG owning the ventilator IP while all decision-making occurs abroad can be denied DTA protection, have the patent box revoked with retrospective tax, and be treated as tax-transparent under the Swiss practice on ‘Basisgesellschaften’ (Art. 21 DBG / treaty abuse para. 2); the Swiss QDMTT and OECD minimum tax further require substance for intra-group allocation of profits

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of ventilators sales from the accounts, fake intercompany invoices, extensive use of cash transactions or second set of books
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative surcharge up to 3 times the evaded federal tax plus cantonal tax surcharge; procedural fines up to CHF 1,000; late interest at 3% p.a.; in aggravated cases (forgery of titles), a criminal conviction for tax fraud (Art. 186 DBG) with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns are subject to personal criminal fines and imprisonment; the veil is pierced (Durchgriff) only on proof of abuse (asset commingling, undercapitalization), exposing board members to unlimited civil restitution for unpaid company taxes; a travel ban is possible under StPO Art. 224–225 during a criminal tax investigation

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The AG distributes CHF 2,000,000 in dividends to the non-resident parent without deducting or remitting the 35% WHT, or recharacterized hidden distributions are not reported
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Claim against the AG for 35% of the gross distribution, plus 3% interest and a penalty up to 3 times the tax if omission was willful; liquidation proceedings may be initiated against the company
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Art. 12 VStG the board members and actual managers are personally liable for the unpaid WHT when the company is unable to pay; in criminal cases, custodial sentences up to 3 years apply and the responsible CFO is barred from future board mandates by registration authorities

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Foreign parent routes ICU ventilator sales through a one-desk Swiss AG with no staff, operations or patents, in order to obtain the 0%/5% dividend WHT rate and the patent box
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits and reclassification of the AG as a sheltered vehicle: full 35% WHT on deemed distributions, participation and patent box relief withdrawn retroactively, plus late interest and evasion surcharge up to 3 times
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the omitted substance entity face criminal liability for false declarations; personal assets can be attached for the unpaid balance where funds were diverted to the parent; a Swiss exit ban and extradition request can be issued in cases of organized tax fraud

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Sale of invasive ventilator units to a related Hong Kong/China distributor at 20% below cost, or payment of excessive royalties for the parent's brand while accumulating losses in Switzerland
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax assessment corrected to arm's-length profits under Art. 58 DBG, with late payment interest of 3%; documentation failure: fine up to CHF 10,000 and the burden of proof shifts against the taxpayer; deliberate sham pricing attracts the 3x evasion surcharge
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The CFO and CEO who knowingly signed the intercompany contracts become personally liable for the resulting underpaid tax under the Swiss Code of Obligations tightening (Art. 754 OR); criminal conviction for tax fraud; travel bans in the criminal phase
